html:
The Almohad Caliphate was a Berber Muslim empire that ruled North Africa and Muslim Spain from 1130 to 1269. At its height it held the whole Maghreb, from Morocco to Libya, and al-Andalus. It is shown here in 1200. On the chart it shares a bar with the Almoravids: Almoravids and Almohads.

Its founder, Ibn Tumart, was a preacher from the Masmuda Berbers of the Atlas who called for strict belief in the oneness of God; the Almohads, al-Muwahhidun, are "those who affirm unity". He attacked the Almoravids as lax. His successor Abd al-Mumin took Marrakesh in 1147 and named himself caliph.

The Almohads built the Kutubiyya mosque in Marrakesh and the Giralda tower in Seville. The philosopher Averroes served at their court, though their rule could also be harsh to Jews and Christians. In 1212 a Christian alliance crushed them at the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa, and their empire fell apart. The Marinids took Marrakesh in 1269.
